fields.meta_title: Customer Satisfaction Survey: Free CSAT Template | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a customer satisfaction survey that asks the right question at the right moment and alerts an owner on every low rating. Free to start.
fields.hero_description: Describe what you want to measure. Emergent builds the CSAT, NPS, and CES questions, the follow-ups by score, and a live dashboard, with every response in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Everything a Customer Satisfaction Survey Needs
fields.features_subheading: CSAT, NPS, CES, or all three. Emergent builds the questions, the branching by score, the alerts, and the database behind them.
fields.feature_1:
CSAT, NPS, CES, and open text in one survey

Every question type satisfaction research uses: a 1-5 CSAT scale, a 0-10 NPS question, a 1-7 CES scale, and open follow-ups. Add or remove a question by describing it.
fields.feature_2:
Every response tied to the customer

Pass the customer ID, account, plan, or ticket ID with the survey link and every response is saved with that context. A low CSAT score becomes an account your team can call today.
fields.feature_3:
Follow-up questions that change by score

Promoters get a review request, passives a feature question, and detractors an open follow-up. CSAT and effort scores branch the same way, set in one line of the prompt.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts on low scores

A Slack alert on every detractor, a HubSpot task on every low CSAT, and an email to the owner for key accounts. Every alert carries the score, the comment, and the customer.
fields.feature_5:
A live CSAT, NPS, and CES dashboard

Generated with the survey and reading from the response database. Filter by segment, plan, or time window, and share one live view with your team instead of a monthly report.
fields.feature_6:
Responses in a database you own

Every response lands in a table in your project, with no response cap. The survey, the dashboard, and every historical response export to GitHub on paid plans whenever you want.

fields.usecase_heading: Satisfaction Surveys You Can Build in Minutes
fields.tab_content_1:
Spot a slipping account long before renewal

New accounts answer a CSAT rating and an effort question on day 7, day 30, and day 90, plus one open follow-up. Answers are saved with the plan and the customer success manager who owns the account. When a score drops to 2, the CSM gets the comment in Slack next to the earlier scores.
fields.tab_content_2:
Reviews from happy buyers, exchanges for the rest

A week after delivery, the buyer rates the product and the delivery out of five stars and can leave a comment. A 5 on the product sends a link to post a public review. A rating of 2 or lower flags the order for the returns team with the comment and order number attached.
fields.tab_content_3:
Per-account scores in HubSpot before every QBR

Each quarter, every contact at a B2B account rates CSAT and NPS for their product line and can add a comment. Scores roll up by account beside last quarter's, and a short summary lands on the HubSpot company record. When an account's NPS falls sharply, the account executive gets every comment from it.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every closed ticket scored, sorted by agent

When a ticket closes, the customer gets a single question on a 1-5 scale about the help they received. Each answer is saved with the agent and with how long the ticket stayed open. A score of 2 or lower posts to the support leads' Slack channel with the comment and a link to the ticket.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Customer Satisfaction Survey
fields.howto_description: Pick the metric, tie every answer to the customer, and route low scores to someone who can act. Emergent generates the survey, the follow-ups, the alerts, and the dashboard from one description, with no response cap.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Use CSAT right after a transaction, NPS for loyalty over time, and CES for the effort of a single interaction. Pick one headline metric per survey; asking all three at once costs completions before it adds insight.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send it where the experience just happened: on ticket close, seven days after delivery, at day 30 of onboarding, or at quarter end for B2B accounts. A survey tied to a real moment gets more responses than a long one sent weeks later.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pair the score with one question about why, one segmentation field such as plan or role, and one improvement question. Then branch on the answer: a 5 can lead to a review request, while a 1 or 2 opens a box asking what went wrong.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Tie every response to the customer
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which fields travel with the link before anything goes out: account ID and plan for SaaS, order number for retail, ticket ID for support. Those fields let the dashboard split scores by segment and let every alert name the account behind the number.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a customer satisfaction survey for my customers.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Route low scores to an owner
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who hears about which score before launch. A detractor at a key account might email its owner, while a low ticket rating goes to the support lead in Slack. Name one person per alert and agree how fast they reply.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Emergent generates the survey with its branching and alerts, plus a dashboard for each score, all reading from a response database you own. Link it from your app or emails, or publish it on your own domain (included in Emergent, uses credits).
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the dashboard weekly by segment and product area, follow up on every detractor within a day, and tell customers what changed because of their feedback. Adjust the questions and thresholds by prompting as patterns appear.

plan.angle: Searchers want to know what a customer satisfaction survey is, which questions to ask and how to score CSAT, then want one they can send. Question-list and glossary pages answer the first part and stop. This page answers the questions briefly and then shows four transactional CSAT surveys where each answer is saved with its account, order or ticket and a low score reaches a named owner: onboarding touches, post-purchase ratings, quarterly B2B account scores and closed support tickets. The feedback-survey sibling owns open-ended comments; the NPS and effort pages own those scores.
tab_stories: Acme Corp rates CSAT and effort at day 7, day 30 and day 90, and when its day 90 score drops to 2 the customer success manager sees the comment in Slack next to the earlier scores, months before renewal.
A buyer rates running shoes and delivery a week after they arrive; a 5 on the product sends a review link, and a 2-star sizing complaint flags the order for the returns team.
Each quarter every contact at a B2B account scores CSAT and NPS, results roll up by account next to last quarter's, and Initech's sharp NPS drop sends every comment to its account executive.
A closed ticket triggers a single 1-5 question, scores feed an average per agent for the week, and a 2 on a billing ticket posts to the support leads' channel with a link to the ticket.

claims_to_source: CSAT is usually asked on a 1-5 scale and the score is the share of 4 and 5 answers
NPS asks how likely a customer is to recommend you on a 0-10 scale; 9-10 are promoters, 7-8 passives, 0-6 detractors
CES asks how easy an interaction was, on a 1-5 or 1-7 scale
